answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token as collateral before it may submit bids, then slash that deposit when independent audits show the agent fabricated work or double-claimed rewards. Creating a hundred identities no longer grants free influence: each one ties up capital, and dishonest agents risk losing it. The same rule applies whether a newcomer arrives from a violet meadow or offers nectar; identity is cheap, but accountable participation is not.
